description: Golden input -> face_id vectors for the canonical encoding frozen in contracts/schemas/face-record.schema.json (issue #34). Every implementation in every language must reproduce both columns. `preimage_utf8_hex` is the hex of the exact UTF-8 bytes that get hashed; it is here rather than only the digest because a digest mismatch says nothing about WHICH field diverged, and the pre-image says exactly.
number_format: RFC 8785 / ECMAScript Number::toString; exponent notation is refused, not written

vectors.name: still-frame-time-null
vectors.why: The still case. frame_time is null and contributes the EMPTY field, so the byte string carries two separators in a row. Nothing else in the tuple can produce an empty field, and a rendered time always contains a '/', so the two cases can never be confused.

vectors.name: video-ntsc-rate
vectors.why: 60000/1001 has no exact float form. It renders as the shortest decimal that round-trips -- identical under Python's repr and JavaScript's String -- and NOT as a rounded 59.94, which would collide two different rates.

vectors.name: video-integral-time-as-int
vectors.why: THE PAIR THAT MATTERS. This vector and the next differ only in whether the JSON writes the time as an integer or as a float with a zero fraction. They MUST produce the same id: it is the exact shape that broke the model config digest, where Python wrote 1.0 and JavaScript wrote 1.

vectors.name: video-integral-time-as-float
vectors.why: The twin of video-integral-time-as-int, written as 1001.0 and 30.0. Same id, or the encoding is not language-independent.

vectors.name: bbox-on-the-half-quantum
vectors.why: 0.30025 * 10000 is EXACTLY 3002.5 as a double. Half away from zero gives 3003, which is what JavaScript's Math.round and Rust's f64::round produce; Python's round() gives 3002, because it rounds half to even. 8855 of the 10000 half-quantum positions in [0,1] are exactly representable, so this is a reachable divergence rather than a theoretical one.

vectors.name: bbox-covers-the-whole-frame
vectors.why: The extremes of the coordinate range: a box at the origin covering the entire oriented frame quantises to 0,0,10000,10000. Confirms the quantum applies to the normalised value and not to a pixel count.

vectors.name: bbox-below-the-quantum
vectors.why: A box narrower than one quantum. It quantises to 0, which is correct and harmless -- a face 0.004% of the frame across is not embeddable anyway -- but it is written down so that nobody 'fixes' it into a floor of 1 and renames every such face.

vectors.name: detector-version-bump-issues-a-new-id
vectors.why: Identical to still-frame-time-null apart from the detector version. A different id is the point: a detector upgrade moves boxes by a pixel or two, and keeping the old id would attach v2's box to v1's embedding.

vectors.name: detector-swap-issues-a-new-id
vectors.why: Identical to still-frame-time-null apart from the model. Two detectors that happen to agree on a box to within the quantum are still two different measurements, and the licence-clean YuNet path exists precisely so that swap can happen.
